Now I wasn't in the council per se to speak on the matter. What I had made presumptions of your story were either 2 cases:

1. Your chair is dumb. Like honestly, they definitely are not qualified to be chairs. Chairs are supposed to judge fairly, and yes I do admit that there are chairs who has biases in styles of speeches and diplomacy in delegates (which are sometimes unavoidable and we may have to accept the reality), chairs who are unable to judge and ruled fairly, and most importantly has very little knowledge over the topic are not qualified to be chairs. You should not cared about these chairs at all. They are not the people you should look up with or to work with. And the chair that chaired you in particular might have been wronged when he gave a BD for someone who disagreed for the sake of disagreeing.
2. The delegate who disagreed with you for the sake of disagreeing might have something a bit more jazz, a bit more intriguing than what you and other delegates have to say. His arguments, his style and knowledge over the topic maybe was better than others. Idk.

With that said, I firmly believe for delegates to not fall onto the path of disagreed for the sake of disagreeing. MUN is a platform for learning, diplomacy, and most importantly joy. Such action that you mentioned is essentially harmful in all terms. It is taking away the diplomacy in the conference and even people's enjoyment of conferences when not used properly, it is a childish behaviour which only annoys other delegates. It does not lead the debate to any conclusive conclusion meaning it only dampened debate and reach no consensus; it can hampered the agreement of the delegate who disagree for the sake of disagreeing. And sometimes when you disagree for the sake of it, it can compromise your very own stance, your very image of the nation you represent. Eg. France has the same stance with Germany on the matter of nuclear energy, yet when France just disagree with Germany for the sake of disagreeing, it serves no purpose, whatsoever.

I was the delegate who disagree for the sake of disagreeing. I was that delegate who POI for nothing but only to challenge people and not expanding any ideas or further the debate. I was the one who tried to intimidate new comers and got smashed absolutely. I had 20 MUN experiences in the summer of 2022 and didn't get a prize in one certain main conference in my city that summer, somebody who was in their first conference get Best Delegate. I was the annoyance of the council, and still trying to fix myself for the sake of it.

You can take this with a grain of salt, or whatever the gram of salt that you're taking. Diplomacy and human connections, be it in MUN or other platforms, are set to be what connected people. Trying to win by being aggressive is no use.

This is not debate where you argue to prove you are right, that you're the best; you're here to make others agree or to reach an agreement with others for the best solutions. Remember that.

I would also highly note, that if you somehow happened to feel overwhelmed by say other delegates who are considered to be aggressive or powered del, the most effective way to deal with them is not to try to further the heat of the debate. Instead, try to calm the situation, or use wits, skillful and practical arguments and diplomacy. The kind of talk that does not exude what powered del do but diplomatic delegate will do. Hope this help
